standard.title: Guidelines for De-icing System for Hydraulic Installations (First Revision)
standard.sector: Water Resources / Hydraulic Gates and Valves

sectional_committee.name: Hydraulic Gates and Valves Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies guidelines, operational parameters, and structural design criteria for de-icing systems (particularly compressed air bubbler systems) installed on hydraulic structures—such as spillway gates, radial gates, fixed-wheel gates, and trash-rack structures—in cold and sub-freezing regions to prevent ice formation and ensure trouble-free gate operation.
standard.scope: This standard specifies guidelines, operational parameters, and structural design criteria for de-icing systems (particularly compressed air bubbler systems) installed on hydraulic structures—such as spillway gates, radial gates, fixed-wheel gates, and trash-rack structures—in cold and sub-freezing regions to prevent ice formation and ensure trouble-free gate operation.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 10021:2000 is an engineering guideline and operational code of practice for dam outfitting and hydraulic gates rather than a direct consumer product, it does not carry a mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp. However, compliance with its technical specifications, air-bubble layout schematics, and pressure curve requirements is strictly mandated in public sector hydropower development tenders (under NHPC, SJVN, NEEPCO, etc.) and dam design audits across sub-freezing regions of India (such as Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Sikkim) to ensure structural safety and prevent freezing disasters.
requirements: Requires preparing an operational calibration curve showing compressor discharge pressures for varying reservoir water levels, based on the specific operating characteristics of the compressor, to match changing hydrostatic heads as the reservoir level rises and falls.
The proper use of control valves for both the operating cycle and the shutdown cycle of the de-icing system must be explicitly described in the operating instructions.

Submerged compressed air nozzles are positioned at standard intervals, typically spaced at 3-metre center-to-center distances (3 m ± tolerance) to establish a continuous rising bubble curtain of warm water.
De-icing distribution piping must be securely integrated with trash racks and spillway gate structures to prevent interference with hoisting machinery or rubbish cleaning operations.
